question: My partner and I separated because our relationship broke down. Do I report myself as separated to CRA after just one month apart?
generated_answer:
The CRA considers you separated if you and your spouse or common-law partner are living apart for at least 90 days due to a breakdown in your relationship. This means that if you have been apart for less than 90 days, you are not considered separated for tax purposes.

If you have been apart for 90 days or more, you can report yourself as separated to the CRA. You will need to complete and submit form RC65, Marital Status Change, to the CRA. This form will help the CRA update your marital status and adjust any tax benefits or credits you may be eligible for.

It's important to note that even if you are separated, you may still be considered common-law for tax purposes if you have lived together for 12 consecutive months in a relationship that is like a marriage. In this case, you would need to report your common-law status to the CRA.

If you are unsure about your situation, it's best to consult with a tax professional or contact the CRA directly for guidance.

Here is a link to the CRA's official page on marital status change: [https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/forms-publications/forms/rc65.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/forms-publications/forms/rc65.html) 

Remember, it's essential to report any changes in your marital status to the CRA as soon as possible to avoid any potential issues with your tax returns. 

If you have any further questions or need additional clarification, please don't hesitate to ask.
